doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Chuck Mangione's legacy at Eastman
summary: Rowe and Jenkins briefly discuss Chuck Mangione's role in the Eastman jazz legacy.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: I got to play, when I was in high school in Rochester, Chuck Mangione led — it was sort of an all-county thing.
And this was before he became — I wonder if he’s — does he have a legacy at Eastman of a sort?

To a degree. Yeah. I think so. We’re respectful of him. I don’t really know him. But he had a hand in getting things going I think. I do. And his brother Gap. No you can’t take that away. And he played — Chuck Mangione played with Blakey.
And Cannonball discovered them — the jazz brothers. Cannonball brought them into Riverside Records. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
Yeah. He did the pop thing and all that but he definitely was a part of the Eastman jazz legacy.
